subject: general
question: Who among the following was the first sultan of Delhi Sultanate to visit the Ajmer shrine of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Muhammad bin Tughlaq**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** was the first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate to visit the Ajmer shrine of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti.
 
• He ruled the Delhi Sultanate from **1325 to 1351** and was the second ruler of the Tughlaq dynasty.
 
• Muhammad bin Tughlaq had a deep interest in Sufism and is known for his patronage of Sufi saints.
 
• The Ajmer shrine, also known as the **Dargah of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti**, is a prominent pilgrimage site for followers of Sufism and Islam.
 
• The visit symbolized the Sultan’s respect for the Chishti Sufi order, which played a significant role in the spiritual and cultural history of medieval India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti:**

 
 
• He was a renowned Sufi saint and founder of the Chishti Order in India.
 
• Known as "Gharib Nawaz" (Benefactor of the Poor), his teachings emphasized love, tolerance, and openness.
 
• His dargah in Ajmer is one of the most significant Sufi shrines in the world.
 
 
 
• **Sufism in India:**
 
 
• Sufism is the mystical dimension of Islam, focusing on inner spirituality and devotion to God.
 
• The Chishti Order was one of the most prominent Sufi orders in medieval India, emphasizing service to humanity.
 
 
 
• **Muhammad bin Tughlaq’s Reign:**
 
 
• He is often remembered for his ambitious but failed projects, including the transfer of the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad.
 
• His administration was marked by a mix of innovation and impracticality.
 
 
 
• **Delhi Sultanate:**
 
 
• The Delhi Sultanate (1206–1526) was a Muslim kingdom based in Delhi that ruled over large parts of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It was established after the defeat of the Rajput ruler Prithviraj Chauhan by Muhammad Ghori in the Second Battle of Tarain.
